title: Red carpet looks: Lindsey Vonn, Eileen Gu, Alysa Liu, other athletes attend 2026 Met Gala
content:
The Met Gala: A night for stars you adore, and dozens of others you’ve never heard of, to strut the red carpet in themed luxury wear. This year’s event again featured a long list of fashion-minded athletes trading in their cleats and sneakers for something a little less comfortable.

It all kicks off the spring exhibit at the Costume Institute at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. A ticket to last year’s Met Gala would have run you a paltry $75,000. This year? Bump that price tag up to a cool $100,000, fit costs not included.

The 2025 event featured Los Angeles Lakers star LeBron James as an honorary chair, while Formula One ace Lewis Hamilton was a co-chair. This year, they had tennis legend Venus Williams as a co-chair (alongside Beyoncé, Nicole Kidman and Anna Wintour), and the Las Vegas Aces’ Aja Wilson was on the host committee.

This year’s theme is “Costume Art,” and the dress code is “Fashion Is Art.”

As someone who saw and really enjoyed “Devil Wears Prada 2” just last night, I feel fully qualified for this assignment. Now, let’s take a look at some of the biggest sports figures in attendance.

We’ll start with Williams herself. She sparkled in a black Swarovski gown, inspired by her portrait at the National Portrait Gallery. Her neckpiece made the ensemble. In a red carpet interview with La La Anthony for Vogue, Williams said it was an adaptation of Wimbledon’s Venus Rosewater Dish trophy, which is named after her. It was embellished with designs referencing her family members and West African heritage.

Williams’ sister Serena Williams, who co-chaired the 2019 gala, also showed out in a silver gown and a right leg wrapped in golden branches, reminiscent of a gladiator sandal.

Wilson went all gold, fingers and hair included. It was elegant and featured its own standout neckpiece.

Quarterback Russell Wilson and Ciara showed up in gold of their own. They seemed bird-themed? Probably not for the Seattle Seahawks, though. There’s your out-of-date sports drama reference of the night.

Alpine skier Lindsey Vonn also hit the red carpet, just a bit over two months after suffering a brutal leg injury during a crash at the Milan Cortina Olympics.

Another Olympic star, skier Eileen Gu, wore a short dress that appeared to be inspired by a bubble bath. Her platinum heels looked particularly hard to walk in, at least to this reporter.

We also had American Olympic breakout Alysa Liu, who went strapless with a heavy dose of scarlet ruffles.

I truthfully have no idea what Naomi Osaka was going for, but it was pretty rad. She looked like a snowbank with small red tree saplings poking through. And if you think the outfit was cool, check out her reveal.

WNBA star Angel Reese, fresh off her blockbuster trade to the Atlanta Dream, rocked a pink, off-the-shoulder gown and a giant diamond necklace.

Fellow WNBA standout Paige Bueckers opted for a suit over a dress. It was black and covered in Jackson Pollock-esque paint splatters.

Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow traded in orange for this blue number, sans designer shades. He stopped to pose alongside Minnesota Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson, whose suit was more traditionally tuxedo-like.

Connor Storrie, one of the leads in the queer hockey phenomenon Heated Rivalry, made an appearance, too. He sported black pants and a white-speckled blouse.

His co-star Hudson Williams was there, too.

Actor Ben Stiller and his wife, Christine Taylor, used their outfit colors to represent the New York Knicks, who opened their second-round playoff series against the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday night. Stiller made a point to call the series outcome, saying, “Knicks in six.” He delivered that prediction to La La Anthony, the ex-wife of Carmelo Anthony. Poetic.

The Golden State Warriors’ Jimmy Butler wore whatever this is.

Dwyane Wade also went all-black, but his jacket served more as an accessory alongside his sheer top. “Look, muscles!” he (probably) said.

Russell Westbrook of the Sacramento Kings likewise forgot a shirt but remembered his gems.

Would any gathering of the hyper-rich be complete without a sports franchise investor? Here’s supermodel Karlie Kloss, one of the pocketbooks behind the New York Liberty. She was dressed as the world’s most expensive, mid-straining ball of mozzarella.

Whatever your thoughts on ballet are, Misty Copeland is a phenomenal athlete who could probably beat you up. Also, did you see her cameo at the Oscars during the performance of Sinners’ “I Lied To You” a few months ago? Executive decision: She makes the list.

Here’s another one you may mock me for including. Dwayne Johnson is a pro wrestler, but again, he could probably beat most people up. That’s athletic enough for me. It was nice seeing him in literally anything other than his wig for the live-action Moana coming out soon.

We also got to see what Super Bowl halftime performer Bad Bunny would look like as one of my ancient Puerto Rican uncles. When La La Anthony asked him how long the makeup took, he said 53 years. He won the night.

There you have it, the Met Gala! Fashion! Sports! All this and more, as always, right here from The Athletic. Thanks for scrolling.
